title: Saitama Stadium: overview

Stadiums are the cathedrals of sport — concrete memory banks where generations experienced the same joys and heartbreaks. This database covers the ground's history, architecture, great events, and how to visit it.

title: History
d: Saitama Stadium opened in 2001. Japan's great football cauldron..
definition: Saitama Stadium opened in 2001. Japan's great football cauldron..
description: The history of Saitama Stadium begins in 2001. Japan's great football cauldron. Like all great grounds, it has been rebuilt, renamed, and reborn — stands rising where terraces stood, roofs arriving decades after the first kick. Its timeline is the timeline of its tenants' triumphs and the city's love affair with the game.

title: Architecture
d: Saitama Stadium holds about 63,700 spectators in its current configuration.

description: The architecture of Saitama Stadium: a 63,700-capacity bowl designed to trap noise and frame the action. Great stadium design balances sightlines, acoustics, and atmosphere — the steepest stands feel closest, the roofs hold the roar in. Renovations keep adding hospitality while trying not to dilute the soul.

title: The tenants

definition: Saitama Stadium is home to Urawa Red Diamonds.

When the team thrives the stadium shakes; when it struggles the old ground groans with it. You cannot separate the venue from its people.

definition: Saitama Stadium's biggest crowds and what drew them.

Capacity has changed with all-seater conversions and expansions, so records from different eras are not directly comparable. What endures is the noise: full houses here are famously loud.
